tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Begin with the README and AGENTS.md to understand the project's purpose as a Voxel Blade damage calculator and build optimizer, its Svelte 5 + TypeScript + Vite tech stack, and the high-level project structure.

tour.title: Application Entry Point
tour.description: The SPA boots from index.html, which loads src/main.ts. main.ts mounts the App component to #app using the Svelte 5 mount() API and initializes Vercel Analytics. The global CSS in app.css defines design tokens and theme overrides.
tour.languageLesson: Svelte 5 replaced the classic `new App({ target })` constructor with a new `mount()` function imported from `svelte`. This is the recommended mounting API for Svelte 5 applications and returns a component handle rather than relying on constructor-based instantiation.

tour.title: Main Application Component
tour.description: App.svelte (~4431 lines) is the monolithic main UI component. It contains the weapon builder with drag-and-drop armor/ring slots, grid-based weapon part dragging, enchantment management, corruption controls, modal dialogs, fuzzy search, and detail cards. It orchestrates all child components.

tour.title: Core Damage Calculation Engine
tour.description: The engine directory contains the heart of the application: calcBuild accumulates equipment stats, applies enchantments, perks, CDR, boosts, and produces the final BuildResult. Sub-modules handle shrine multipliers, weapon calculations (standard + monk), enchantment application with slot enforcement, and damage type bonuses from perks like Void Rage and Emotional.
tour.languageLesson: The engine uses a pipeline pattern: equipment stats are accumulated into a StatMap, then enchantments modify it via selectors/multipliers/additives, shrine tier scales everything, and perks finalize with effectiveness multipliers. Functions operate on plain data structures (not classes), making composition straightforward and testing easy.

tour.title: Game Data Definitions and Constants
tour.description: Game data lives in src/data/ as JSON files (weapons, armor, perks, enchantments, races, guilds, runes, rings) and TypeScript modules that define buffs, DoT damage, boosts, weapon arts, draconic mechanics, and stat conversions. The constants in src/lib/constants/ provide numerical values for all game mechanics: damage types, crit, cooldowns, defense, thresholds, and storage keys.

tour.title: State Management with Svelte Stores
tour.description: Application state is managed via Svelte writable stores in store.ts. The `build` store holds the entire BuildState (race, guild, equipment, enchantments, buffs) and persists to localStorage. A derived `result` store automatically recomputes BuildResult whenever the build changes, powering all downstream UI.

tour.title: Damage Analysis and Computation
tour.description: DamageAnalyzer.svelte (~7385 lines, the largest file) computes the full damage breakdown: weapon M1/M2 hits, weapon arts, rune damage, perk damage, DoT scaling, type resolution, defense/compliance, buff/debuff toggles, healing analysis, and stat efficiency. BaseDamageCalc.svelte handles per-hit pre-mitigation damage computation with armor penetration and effective defense.

tour.title: Buff, Debuff, and Perk Interaction Components
tour.description: BuffList.svelte displays active buffs from items, perks, potions, weapon arts, and draconic infusion with potency/duration sliders and debuff toggles. CdrStepsCalc.svelte visualizes cooldown reduction as a chain of operations. PropellingFunTracker.svelte and EmotionalTracker.svelte handle specific perk-state toggles.

tour.title: Selection Modals and Search UI
tour.description: Modals for selecting races, guilds, armor, weapon parts, and accessories live in src/lib/modals/. Each provides search filtering, stat/perk preview, and fuzzy matching. The ModalSearchHeader component combines search input, tag filters, stat filters, and sort buttons into a reusable modal header. SuggestDrop and DidYouMean provide autocomplete and correction suggestions.

tour.title: Build Persistence and Sharing
tour.description: BuildSaves.svelte manages up to 100 save slots with drag-reordering, base64 compressed export/import, duplicate detection, inline name editing, and localStorage persistence. Build states are minified and key-mapped for compact shareable strings.
tour.languageLesson: The export system uses key minification (SAVE_KEY_MAP mapping full property names like 'bladeName' to short keys like 'bN') combined with JSON.stringify and btoa compression. This pattern is common in web game tools to produce shareable URL-friendly build codes.

tour.title: Reusable UI Component Library
tour.description: A library of generic UI primitives under src/lib/ui/ provides consistent Badge, Button, Card, Divider, Panel, Section, Stat, and animated RollValue components used throughout the application. These follow a consistent variant-based theming system with color accents.

tour.title: Tests and Tooling Configuration
tour.description: Unit tests in tests/piercer.test.ts validate the Piercer perk conditional boost and true damage conversion logic using Vitest. The project is configured with TypeScript (strict mode), Vite with Svelte plugin and PWA support, Vercel deployment, and Fallow static analysis for dead-code and security checks.
